messages:
Alex Kline: Heads up — since ~09:10 we see a big retry/5xx spike on the infer-gpu-spot service. p50 latency doubled and clients are hitting connect timeouts. Noticed IPVS endpoint hits are super skewed to 2 pods.
Infra Oncall Bot: Alert: default/infer-gpu-spot high-5xx-rate (90m) — triggered 09:12 — incidents dashboard: https://ops/redwood/alerts/12345
Maria Chen: thx. Alex can you paste the svc/namespace and a quick ipvs / endpoints dump?
Alex Kline: default/infer-gpu-spot. grabbing ipvs stats and endpoint list now.
Alex Kline: ipvs stats show this (trimmed):
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.0.12.34:9090 rr
  -> 10.1.4.11:9090               Masq    1      0          123
  -> 10.1.4.12:9090               Masq    1      0          42
  -> 10.1.4.13:9090               Masq    1      0          9800
```
Juan Perez: wow that is insane skew. looks like one endpoint is taking ~99% of the traffic.
Olivia Park: can you `kubectl get endpoints -o wide` for that svc? need to confirm pod IPs + node.
Alex Kline: pasted endpoint list:
```
NAME                 ENDPOINTS                         AGE
infer-gpu-spot       10.1.4.11:9090,10.1.4.12:9090,10.1.4.13:9090   3d
```
and node mapping: 10.1.4.13 is on node gpu-14, the other two on gpu-02 and gpu-03. gpu-14 shows much higher CPU on kube-proxy and nv peer traffic.
Samir Patel: any chance of conntrack/NAT table entries getting stuck? ipvs uses destination hashing but conntrack can cause stickiness. can we check `conntrack -L | grep 10.1.4.13 | wc -l`?
Maria Chen: I ran conntrack dump — ~18k ESTABLISHED entries pointing to 10.1.4.13. others only few hundreds.
Juan Perez: that smells like asymmetric forwarding or hairpinning loop where backend keeps getting reselected. Are we running UDP or TCP? gRPC streaming over TCP.
Olivia Park: also saw kernel logs on gpu-14 around 09:05: `mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: Link down, forcing fallback to TCP/IP` and RDMA stack warnings — could be NIC flapping and causing fallback so one node handles more of the traffic after route changes.
Alex Kline: good catch — dmesg excerpt:
```
[09:05:11] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: NIC link status changed: DOWN
[09:05:12] rdma: IB device mlx5_0 (gpu-14) down, falling back to sfnoffload
[09:06:00] kernel: ipvs: scheduler rr: picked 10.1.4.13 many times
```
Maria Chen: If RDMA/UCX fallback triggered, that can increase latency and cause upstream retries; but doesn't explain skew unless routing weights got recomputed. Need kube-proxy mode and kernel ipvs settings.
Samir Patel: kube-proxy is in IPVS mode on these nodes. We pushed a kube-proxy update last week that changed `--ipvs-scheduler=rr` to default; maybe a regression in stickiness handling.
Juan Perez: also check `sysctl net.ipv4.fib_multipath_hash_seed` and NIC multipath settings — different hash seed on gpu-14 could bias local hashing.
Alex Kline: ran `ipvsadm -Ln --get` on gpu-14 vs gpu-02,03 — gpu-14 had different local address ordering and kernel reports: `ip_vs: rehash failed` around 09:06 on gpu-14.
Maria Chen: can we repro quickly by curling with high concurrency from a pod on same node vs remote node to see hairpin behavior?
Alex Kline: started a 1000-rps test from a client pod on node client-07: results show 85% of connections still end up at 10.1.4.13. Test from node client-09 (same rack as gpu-02) spreads more evenly.
Olivia Park: that implies node-local preference / L3 path difference. Are we using node-local externalTrafficPolicy or endpoint-slice locality?
Samir Patel: service has default externalTrafficPolicy (Cluster). EndpointSlices exist. However, I suspect kernel hash + NIC failover + RDMA fallback mutated the forwarding table so one node's local IPVS table started favoring the 10.1.4.13 backend for many hashes.
Juan Perez: short-term mitigation: add temporary weight adjustments to IPVS to force even distribution: `ipvsadm -e -t 10.0.12.34:9090 -r 10.1.4.13:9090 -w 1` (set others to 5) or cordon/gently drain gpu-14 for new connections.
Maria Chen: I bumped weights to balance (set 10.1.4.13 -> 1, others -> 4) and scaled up extra pods on gpu-02. Monitoring now.
Alex Kline: after weight bump p50 latency dropped ~30% and retry rate decreased. still seeing a small tail.
Olivia Park: we should also investigate firmware/NIC team — RDMA fallbacks are scary for throughput on GPU nodes. logging a ticket.
Infra Oncall Bot: Incident note auto-created — ticket INF-2026-823 created for NIC/RDMA fallback investigation.
Samir Patel: follow-up action items: 1) collect kernel ipvs/ipvs_syncd logs from gpu-14 for 09:00-09:30; 2) run `ethtool -S` and mlx5 counters; 3) rollback kube-proxy build if we see similar in other clusters; 4) consider enabling IPVS persistent-conn timeout tuning.
Juan Perez: + add a small e2e test in infra CI to simulate NIC link flaps and ensure ipvs rehash behaves.
Maria Chen: I'll pull ipvs kernel debug logs and send to eng-runtime and NIC vendor. tagging @Olivia and @Samir.
Alex Kline: thanks all. keeping weight change for 30m then we'll drain gpu-14 and repro in staging. :thumbsup:
Olivia Park: quick note — if we see conntrack spikes repeatedly, we should raise NAT table size to avoid evictions during failovers.
Samir Patel: agreed. logging follow-up tasks in the incident ticket.
Alex Kline: update at 09:47 — retry rate back to baseline, p50 stable. leaving ticket open for root cause.
